card.title: Modern Periodic Law and Modern Periodic Table

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The modern periodic law re-founds Mendeleev's table on **atomic number**: properties are a periodic function of Z (Moseley, 1913), because electronic configurations — the true cause of chemical behaviour — repeat at regular intervals of Z. Every mass-based anomaly dissolves: Te (Z = 52) precedes I (Z = 53), Ar (18) precedes K (19), and all isotopes share one position.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Modern periodic law: properties ∝ f(atomic number Z) - Period = highest occupied n; Group = outer e⁻ (s/p block), outer s e⁻ + 10 (d block) - Shell capacity 2n²; groups 18, periods 7

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Z vs A:** atomic **number** (protons) orders the table; atomic **mass number** (protons + neutrons) does not — that was Mendeleev's error.  ·  **Group of d-block elements:** count s electrons + 10, not s + d electrons (Sc: 4s²3d¹ is group 3, not 3).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The physical and chemical properties of the elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers." — the Modern Periodic Law.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Tellurium before iodine*** — by mass 127.6 > 126.9 would put Te after I, breaking the chemical pattern; by Z (52 < 53) Te precedes I and the pattern holds — the anomaly that proved the modern law.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: NEB 2021 3m — three differences, modern vs Mendeleev (table above); NEB 2024 3m — period and group of Z = 19, 20, 31, 36, 55 (table above). Other items are NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — From Atomic Mass to Atomic Number Mendeleev arranged elements by **atomic mass** and left brilliant gaps — but mass-based ordering put tellurium (127.6) before iodine (126.9) and stacked argon against potassium wrongly. Moseley's X-ray work (1913) gave each element a true serial number — the **atomic number Z** — and the modern periodic law re-founded the table on it.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The Modern Periodic Law **"The physical and chemical properties of the elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers."** - Atomic number Z = number of protons = the element's true identity. - Properties repeat because **electronic configurations repeat**: each new shell begins a new period, and elements with the same outer-shell configuration land in the same group.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Z decides, configuration places." Period = highest n; group = outer e⁻ (+10 if d-block). Mendeleev-vs-modern: mass→Z, anomalies→none, isotopes→one place, cause→configuration.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2021 (3m): How does the Modern Periodic Law differ from Mendeleev's Periodic Law? State any three points of difference.** — (1) Basis: Mendeleev orders by **atomic mass**; the modern law orders by **atomic number**.…  ·  **NEB 2024 (3m): Identify the elements with atomic numbers 19, 20, 31, 36 and 55, and state the period and group of each in the long form of the periodic table.** — 19: K, [Ar]4s¹ → period 4, group 1. 20: Ca, [Ar]4s² → period 4, group 2. 31: Ga, [Ar]4s²3d¹⁰4p¹ → period 4, group 13. 36: Kr, [Ar]4s²3d¹⁰4p⁶ → period 4, group 18.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For the law-contrast question, answer in numbered rows (basis: Mendeleev vs modern) — NEB awards per contrast, not per paragraph. Always name the anomaly (Te/I or Ar/K) as evidence.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Configuration → position:** write the electronic configuration and read off period (highest n), block (last-entering subshell) and group (outer electrons, +10 for d-block). This one skill answers every "locate the element" question.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Modern law: properties are a periodic function of atomic number (Moseley, 1913). Cause: repeating outer electronic configurations. Long form: 18 groups, 7 periods, s/p/d/f blocks. Mass anomalies (Te/I, Ar/K) and isotope placement resolve automatically.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Moseley was killed at Gallipoli in 1915 at age 27; scientists called it the war's greatest loss to science — he had just given the periodic table its true foundation.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): State the Modern Periodic Law and name the scientist whose work established it.** — "Physical and chemical properties of the elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers" — established by **H. G. J. Moseley (1913)** through X-ray spectral studies.  ·  **NEB-style (2m): An element has the configuration [Ar] 4s² 3d¹⁰ 4p³. Give its period, group, block and name.** — Highest n = 4 → period 4; last electron in p → p-block; outer electrons 4s²4p³ = 5 → group 15; the element is **arsenic (As, Z = 33)**.

rows.text: Why did mass-based ordering fail for Ar–K while Z-based ordering succeeds?  ·  An element ends 5s² 4d¹⁰ 5p⁵ — name its period, group and block without looking it up.  ·  Why is periodicity better explained by outer-shell configuration than by atomic mass?

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Periodic function of Z — not of mass:** quoting the modern law with "atomic weight" is an automatic zero; the one word that matters is **atomic number**.  ·  **Period vs group:** period = row = shell being filled (highest n); group = column = outer configuration. Z = 19 and Z = 55 share group 1 but sit in different periods.  ·  **d-block group counting:** for d-block elements group = outer s electrons + 10 (Sc: 4s²3d¹ → group 3; Zn: 4s²3d¹⁰ → group 12).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (2m): Why do properties of elements repeat periodically?** — Because electronic configurations repeat: each period starts filling a new shell, and elements with the same outer-shell configuration (same valence count) show the same chemistry — the cause Mendeleev's law could not…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Where do ¹H, ²H and ³H sit in the modern table and why?** — All three (protium, deuterium, tritium) occupy the single position of hydrogen (Z = 1): the modern law orders by Z, and isotopes differ in mass number, not Z.  ·  **NEB-style (2m): An element has configuration [Ar] 4s² 3d¹⁰ 4p². Give its period, group and block.** — Highest n = 4 → period 4; six outer electrons (4s² 4p²) → group 14; last electron enters p → p-block. (The element is Ge.)
